The Agent Economy: New Paths to Build and Earn

Farshad Tavakoli

Sept 03, 2025

4 min read

With the rise of agentic AI, we are entering an era where digital agents can think, reason, and act with autonomy. These agents are not just responsive assistants waiting for a command; they are proactive collaborators capable of orchestrating workflows, making decisions, and even interacting with other systems and agents on behalf of their users. This shift is more than a technical milestone—it’s the foundation of a new economy built around intelligent, autonomous systems. 

One of the most immediate opportunities lies in creating industry-specific AI agents that solve pressing real-world challenges. In healthcare, agents could streamline patient documentation and billing. In finance, they could help navigate compliance requirements or offer personalized financial guidance. In retail, they might oversee supply chain operations or enhance customer experiences. By embedding deep domain knowledge into autonomous systems, these agents become highly valuable solutions that organizations are willing to adopt through subscription or usage-based models. 

There is also an enormous opportunity to enhance existing platforms by integrating agentic intelligence. A project management tool that can automatically reprioritize tasks as deadlines shift, or a CRM platform that drafts personalized sales outreach, dramatically increases the utility of those products. These kinds of enhancements not only make platforms more competitive but also create natural pathways for premium features and upselling, often doubling or tripling the perceived value of a solution. 

Beyond standalone tools, the emergence of marketplaces for agent skills could mirror the app store revolution that transformed the mobile era. In such ecosystems, individuals and organizations could buy or sell modular agent behaviors, from bookkeeping integrations to SEO optimization skills. This opens the door to scalable, passive income models where reusable components can be deployed across thousands of use cases, creating ongoing streams of revenue for those who design them. 

Another model gaining traction is Agents-as-a-Service (AaaS). Not every business will want to manage the complexity of hosting and maintaining their own AI infrastructure. This creates a demand for hosted, continuously updated agent solutions that can be consumed on a subscription or pay-per-use basis. Imagine an autonomous research agent that monitors industry trends around the clock, or a compliance agent that ensures policies remain aligned with evolving regulations. Delivered as a service, these intelligent systems bring the flexibility and scalability of SaaS, but with proactive, autonomous intelligence at their core. 

Perhaps the most compelling aspect of this emerging economy is the data flywheel effect. As agents carry out tasks, they generate valuable insights into workflows, user behaviors, and bottlenecks. When harnessed ethically and transparently, this data can improve agent performance, fuel new innovations, or be aggregated into anonymized datasets with significant market value. Those who understand how to transform these feedback loops into growth engines will hold a long-term advantage. 

We are still early in the adoption curve of agentic AI, but history offers clear lessons. The mobile app boom created entirely new industries and reshaped old ones. The rise of SaaS turned nimble teams into enterprise giants. Agentic AI now stands poised to do the same, and the opportunities to build and earn within this ecosystem are only beginning to unfold. 

The takeaway is clear: the paths are diverse, from crafting specialized agents to enhancing existing platforms, from launching marketplaces to delivering intelligent services. What unites them is the creativity, execution, and timing required to seize the moment. Those who engage now won’t just benefit from this technological revolution—they will help shape the fabric of the agent economy.
